title: Rama's vow of refuge
hook: Ravana's own brother asks Rama for shelter, and Rama answers with a vow
carry: whoever comes once asking, god shelters
tomorrow: why would a mother ask God to look less like God?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the padukas: two wooden sandals on an empty throne, as Bharata served in his brother's name and waited for him. Rama stays with us one more day, on a beach, at night.

The knock always comes at the worst hour: a text near midnight, a friend on the step with a bag. Rama's comes on a beach. His army is camped on the shore, facing Lanka, and a figure crosses the water through the air with a few companions and calls down. I'm Vibhishana, Ravana's brother. I told him to give Sita back, and he threw me out. I've come to Rama for refuge. The whole camp goes quiet. The enemy's own brother is asking to come in.
screen: `A KNOCK AT THE WORST HOUR.` → `RAVANA'S BROTHER, IN THE SKY.` → `I'VE COME FOR REFUGE.`

segments.voice: In Valmiki's Ramayana, Rama doesn't answer right away. He asks his allies. Sugriva, the monkey king, is wary: this could be a spy, here to learn the plans or strike while they sleep. Others want to test him first, or keep him under guard until the war is won. Every one of those fears is reasonable; it is wartime, and he is Ravana's brother. Hanuman speaks up for him: he chose his moment with care, and he talks like someone who means it. Then Rama answers, and the answer goes past the question. Whoever comes to me even once, he says, and tells me they're mine, I protect from every being. That's my vow. Then he goes further: even if Ravana himself came this way asking, I'd take him in. So Vibhishana is welcomed, and Rama has him anointed, right there, as the future king of Lanka. Here's the part worth telling someone tonight. The camp was asking: is he safe for us? Rama answered a different question: who am I? A refuge that only opens for the safe guest isn't much of a refuge. And a vow that has to be re-voted every night isn't much of a vow. This beach is the root of a big Hindu teaching: sharanagati, taking refuge. Many Vaishnavas, Sri Vaishnavas above all, treasure Rama's vow as God's own promise. You don't earn your way in. Come once, honestly, say I'm yours, and you're held.
screen: `RAMA ASKS HIS ALLIES FIRST.` · `A SPY? OR SOMEONE WHO MEANS IT?` · `ANYONE WHO COMES ONCE, I PROTECT.` · `EVEN RAVANA, IF HE CAME.` · then, large: `SHARANAGATI: COME ONCE, AND BE HELD.`

segments.voice: Fold your hands at your chest, the way Hindus do in front of a shrine: the gesture of someone who has come for refuge. If you pray, say Rama's name softly on each breath out, Ram, the way many Hindus repeat it through the day. If you don't, let the folded hands say it for you: I've come, I'm here. Stay with that for the whole sit.
Rama: the prince of Ayodhya, in the Puranas Vishnu come as a man, whose vow was to shelter anyone who comes asking.
Your line: whoever comes once asking, God shelters. That's sharanagati, and Rama said it would hold even for Ravana. Back tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1555 COUNTS.` → `WHOEVER COMES ONCE ASKING, GOD SHELTERS.` → `TOMORROW: WHY ASK GOD TO LOOK LESS LIKE GOD?`
